facts.text: ISO 21815 is a family of international standards specifying what collision warning or collision avoidance systems on earth-moving machines must do, how they communicate with the machine, and how to determine the distance at which they must act.
facts.quote: ISO 21815 is the family of international standards that says what a collision warning or collision avoidance system on an earth-moving machine must do, how it talks to the machine, and how to work out the distance at which it must act.

facts.text: ISO 21815 comes from International Organization for Standardization committee ISO/TC 127 and covers earth-moving machines defined in ISO 6165, underground mining machines per ISO 19296, and road-construction machines.
facts.quote: It comes from the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) committee ISO/TC 127 and covers earth-moving machines as defined in ISO 6165, underground mining machines per ISO 19296 and road-construction machines

facts.text: ISO 21815 is technology-neutral and prescribes no sensor; its avoidance scope covers speed reduction or motion inhibit, but not automatic steering.
facts.quote: It is technology-neutral (no sensor is prescribed), it covers avoidance "by speed reduction or motion inhibit" but not automatic steering

facts.text: ISO 21815 leaves responsibility for safe operation with the operator.
facts.quote: it leaves responsibility for safe operation with the operator

facts.text: ISO 21815 does not apply to systems installed before its publication.
facts.quote: it does not apply to systems installed before its publication

facts.text: As reported in October 2026, ISO 21815-1:2022, General requirements, was published as edition 1 in January 2022.
facts.quote: | ISO 21815-1:2022 | General requirements | Published, edition 1, January 2022

facts.text: ISO 21815-1 specifies requirements for detecting objects, warning the operator, automatic intervention, and test procedures; the numerical requirements are in paid text that the booklet did not review.
facts.quote: Requirements for detecting objects, warning the operator, intervening automatically, and test procedures (numbers sit in the paid text, not reviewed)

facts.text: As reported in October 2026, ISO/TS 21815-2:2021, On-board J1939 communication interface, was published as a technical specification in July 2021 and confirmed in December 2024.
facts.quote: | ISO/TS 21815-2:2021 | On-board J1939 communication interface | Published technical specification, July 2021; confirmed December 2024

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 defines SAE International J1939 messages—SLOW_DOWN, CONTROLLED-STOP, EMERGENCY-STOP, capability discovery, and keep-alive—through which a collision device (CxD) asks the machine to slow, stop, or stay still; the interface is not intended for plug-and-play.
facts.quote: Defines the SAE International J1939 network messages (SLOW_DOWN, CONTROLLED-STOP, EMERGENCY-STOP, capability discovery, keep-alive) by which a collision device (CxD) asks the machine to slow, stop or stay still; "not intended for plug-and-play"

facts.text: As reported in October 2026, ISO 21815-3:2023, Risk area and risk level for forward and reverse motion, was published as edition 1 in August 2023; the booklet reviewed the 2022 draft.
facts.quote: | ISO 21815-3:2023 | Risk area and risk level for forward and reverse motion | Published, edition 1, August 2023 (the booklet reviewed the 2022 draft)

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 defines the CxS distance as detection, decision, action, and stopping distance plus a safe distance; CxS is the standard's shorthand for a collision warning or avoidance system.
facts.quote: Defines the CxS distance (CxS being the standard's shorthand for a collision warning or avoidance system): detection, decision, action and stopping distance plus a safe distance

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 requires the manufacturer to declare system delays.
facts.quote: the manufacturer must declare system delays

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 provides worked examples for surface and underground machines and is a type-C standard under ISO 12100.
facts.quote: worked examples for surface and underground machines; type-C under ISO 12100

facts.text: As reported in October 2026, ISO 21815-4, Risk area and risk level for swing and rotation, had been under publication at stage 60.00 since September 2026, with publication scheduled for October 2026.
facts.quote: | ISO 21815-4 | Risk area and risk level for swing and rotation | Under publication (stage 60.00) since September 2026; scheduled October 2026

facts.text: ISO 21815-4 addresses rotation of excavators and similar machines using motion inhibit before rotation starts, and expressly excludes avoidance by automatic application of braking.
facts.quote: Rotation of excavators and similar; motion inhibit before rotation starts; expressly "does not cover avoidance by automatic application of the braking"

facts.text: As reported in October 2026, ISO/PRF 21815-5, Risk area and risk level for other forms of motion, had been at proof stage 50.20 since September 2026, with publication scheduled for November 2026.
facts.quote: | ISO/PRF 21815-5 | Risk area and risk level for other forms of motion | Proof stage (50.20) since September 2026; scheduled November 2026

facts.text: ISO/PRF 21815-5 addresses articulation, four-wheel steering, towed trailers in reverse, skid-steer turning, and telescopic and vertical motions.
facts.quote: Articulation, four-wheel steering, towed trailers in reverse, skid-steer turning, telescopic and vertical motions

facts.text: Standards Australia published AS 21815.1:2023 as a modified adoption of ISO 21815-1, but the booklet could not read the modifications.
facts.quote: Standards Australia published AS 21815.1:2023, a modified adoption of Part 1 whose changes the booklet could not read

facts.text: Standards Australia published SA TS ISO 21815.2:2023 for the communication interface; neither SA TS ISO 21815.2:2023 nor AS 21815.1:2023 is law unless incorporated.
facts.quote: and SA TS ISO 21815.2:2023 for the interface; neither is law unless incorporated

facts.text: The booklet found no statements about simulation in the ISO 21815 series.
facts.quote: On simulation the series says nothing that was found.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 relies on calculation of the CxS distance, supporting analytical evidence for stopping-distance margins but not simulation-based acceptance.
facts.quote: Part 3 relies on calculation of the CxS distance, which "supports analytical evidence for stopping-distance margins but is not simulation-based acceptance"

facts.text: ISO 21815-1 and ISO 21815-3 expect physical tests; passing a simulation cannot be declared to satisfy an ISO 21815 physical test.
facts.quote: Parts 1 and 3 expect physical tests, and an ISO 21815 physical test cannot be declared satisfied because a simulation passed

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 notes that false positives could create alarm fatigue.
facts.quote: Part 3 notes that false positives "could create alarm fatigue"

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 assigns setting the safe offset to the authorized person at the worksite, so configurable site parameters must also be validated.
facts.quote: its safe offset is set "by the authorized person" at the worksite, so configurable site parameters must be validated too

facts.text: The booklet concludes that ISO 21815 is the core off-road standard family and was still being completed in October 2026.
facts.quote: ISO 21815 is "the core off-road standard family, and it is still being completed"

facts.text: The booklet's plan uses ISO 21815-3 as its backbone by calculating CxS distance for each machine model from ISO 3450 brake data and declared delays.
facts.quote: The booklet's plan uses Part 3 as the backbone: calculate the CxS distance per machine model from ISO 3450 brake data and declared delays

facts.text: The booklet's plan builds the scenario catalog around ISO 21815-3 risk areas and presents simulation as coverage evidence alongside the physical tests prescribed by the standard.
facts.quote: build the scenario catalog around its risk areas, and present simulation as coverage evidence beside the physical tests the standard prescribes

facts.text: The booklet treats ISO 21815's separate parts for forward and reverse motion, swing, and articulation as evidence that off-road motion types need their own hazard models, helping explain why road scenarios do not transfer directly.
facts.quote: Its separate parts for forward and reverse, swing and articulation are also evidence that off-road motion types need their own hazard models, one reason road scenarios do not transfer directly
